children: Full convergence. Anything not in the manifest is revoked or dropped. This is the standard GitOps model — the manifest is the single source of truth.

content.name: p
children: Only grant, never revoke. New roles, grants, memberships, and default privileges are created, but nothing is removed. This is the safest mode for incremental adoption — start managing roles without risking disruption to existing access.

rule. The rest of the plan still applies, and the run does not fail. Use
when you need those assertions enforced.

role can stay that way during adoption even if a minimal manifest would otherwise imply

children: Manage declared roles fully (including revoking excess grants within their scope), but never drop undeclared roles. This is the middle ground — you get full convergence for roles in the manifest, but roles outside the manifest are left untouched.

attributes.title: Adopt does not preserve undeclared grants

children.name: p
children: Adopt only filters role drops. Every privilege a declared role holds that the manifest does not declare — including out-of-band grants from migrations or manual SQL — is revoked. Review the full plan (
) before applying, and stay in additive mode until the manifest declares everything the database relies on.

when you're confident the manifest is complete.
